title: Frontend: Tree Navigation
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Tree Navigation. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({nodes=[{id:root,title:Root,children:[{id:a,title:A}]}]}). Render a nested disclosure list. Node li[data-node=ID] contains button[data-open=ID] for folders (children array) or [data-select=ID] for files. Folders start collapsed; clicks select and toggle them. [data-testid=selected] displays selected ID or None. Use stable IDs and aria-expanded on folder buttons. This native-disclosure navigation is intentionally not an ARIA tree widget.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Separate expansion, selection, and keyboard focus.
alternativeApproaches: Virtualize a large tree while keeping the visible keyboard order and accessibility relationships correct.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Collapsed children; disabled node; Home/End.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
